notes: The physical sheet bears top number 8 and lower-left number 19, with no date. Its main text gives a presentation in sigma_0, sigma_1, sigma_infinity and rho with relations labelled (4), (5) and (6). The left note adds conjugation relations and states that two generators sigma_0 and rho suffice, with sigma_0^2=rho^3=1. These are the author’s assertions, not results proved by this reader.

The main NB says that imposing sigma_0,sigma_1,sigma_infinity=1 leaves rho^3=1 and draws a conclusion that rho is not a word in the sigma_i; the abbreviated qualifier after un mot remains p.v./p.r. A struck donc is preserved provisionally. The next paragraph relates the notation to earlier relations and cancels a lengthy attempted explanation with primed symbols.

Relation (7) records the exchange of l_j and l_k under int(sigma_i), with a distinctness insertion and a cancelled comment, followed by the action of rho. The insertion physically reads (i,j,k) distincts), with an extra unmatched close. That authorial punctuation is retained. The parenthetical word in the deleted comment remains dernier/devenir.

The final live paragraph asks to explicate epsilon_i with epsilon_i^2=l_i for i=0,1,infinity, describing a generator of the centralizer or normalizer. System(8) has a crossed number and several larger strokes whose exact scope is uncertain, together with local exponent cancellations. The second row’s crossed final l1 inverse is replaced by a separate l1 to the right/below. The third row ends in bare l-infinity. Its first-row last index remains doubtful. There is no authorial date or separate interrogative doubt phrase beyond the aspirational On voudrait and the alternative descriptions in prose.

The parent reader raised a mathematical prompt concerning the initial-rho exponent in the left-margin l_infinity formula. This first reader inspected the existing crop: its thick zigzag favors cancellation of -1, but a live inverse remains possible. No mathematical proof or algebraic computation was performed by this first reader, and no algebra was used to choose the ink state. Any parent algebra check is separate.

Whole page and the two supplied native halves were each viewed once. Twenty-two initial saved crops covered all open or mandatory loci; one additional crop recovered only the previously uncovered ending of the cancelled marginal product. It showed blank space beyond the bracket and excluded the =1 supplied by C. No OCR, external research, other page reading, or TeX compilation was used. Root has inspected all 23 crops.

The product formula remains a whole-formula doubt, with explicit shorter/longer second-bracket alternatives and no terminal =1. The crop of idem slightly clips the initial-i edge; that edge was seen during the native-half reading and the remaining d/e/m strokes identify the word. The manuscript has no isolated full stops where C supplied them after relation (6), the right NB, the last left-margin inner-conjugation formula and the lower formula of (7).

The line count includes both handwritten page numbers, the separate small cancelled i.e. line, interlinear insertion at (7), and each physical formula row. The inventory accounts for every span marked by C and for the newly identified local exponent and replacement layers; C’s blanket system(8) deletion is qualified in the audit. All such spans, all numeral-bearing formulas and all lexical disagreements have complete selected readings in second_boxes.

Main-reader check of the NB: in the presentation consisting of (4)–(6) and the added cyclic conjugation relations, setting all three sigma generators to 1 leaves exactly rho cubed equal to 1. Relation (4) becomes rho to the minus third equal to 1. Thus there is a quotient C3 in which every sigma has trivial image and rho has nontrivial image; rho cannot be a word in those sigma generators. This checks the stated obstruction for sigma generators, not for the later epsilon generators.

The main-reader word certificate check_020_words.py reduces the marginal formulas in the free product generated by s=sigma0 and r=rho, with s squared and r cubed equal to 1.
